long_biography.plain_text:
After a decade in financial-control roles at Continental and General Tire, Schindelhauer joined AIXTRON Semiconductor Technologies as a managing shareholder in 1992. He led the company's stock-market flotation five years later and moved from management into the supervisory board, eventually chairing it. His work linked capital-market development with long-term governance of a supplier to the semiconductor industry.

During a management transition, Schindelhauer temporarily returned as chief executive and finance chief before resuming the supervisory chair. He continued to lead the board until retiring in 2025, closing a relationship with AIXTRON that had lasted more than three decades. Across that period, the company evolved from a specialist German equipment maker into an international supplier of deposition systems used to manufacture semiconductor materials.
